idiom_name: one owned boundary module: local port + adapter + translator + foreign gateway
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give the domain a port whose signatures use only local types; implement it with an adapter that is the sole caller of the upstream; convert whole models in dedicated translator functions instead of scattering field access and unit conversions through the code; and wrap the upstream client in a gateway that owns transport, authentication, timeouts, retries and error mapping. Enforce the rule mechanically - no upstream types, ids or exceptions outside the boundary - and keep validation, resilience and observability at the seam rather than in the domain. The heavier classic form (a facade class plus separate adapter and translator objects) is justified when one boundary is shared by several callers, when the upstream protocol needs a client object with its own lifecycle, or when translation must be injected or swapped; for a single call path, one small module with pure mapping functions and one adapter is the same pattern at lower cost.
code_sketch:
# domain-facing port: local types only
port place_order(Order) -> Receipt or Rejected

# adapter: the only caller of the upstream API
class LegacyOrderAdapter(OrderPort):
    def place_order(order):
        dto  = to_legacy(order)            # translator: pure mapping
        resp = gateway.submit(dto)         # transport, timeouts, retries
        return to_receipt(resp)            # upstream shape -> local types
pitfalls: Letting the adapter return upstream types or raw maps 'for now' - the domain then depends on the foreign model even though the layer exists.
Scattering translation through the codebase: field access, unit conversion and status mapping outside the boundary give the foreign model a second home.
Growing the layer into an application service: orchestration, caching and domain rules make it a second model nobody owns.
No enforcement: without a module dependency rule or a test that fails on foreign imports, the boundary decays one call site at a time.
Treating the layer as free: forgetting timeouts, retries and error translation makes the upstream's failure semantics the domain's problem.
